description: Pull the fields you name from any public page as JSON, each checked against the page. $0.01 for most pages: the page'...

ignoreInvalidURLs.description: Skip addresses that are not public website URLs. Send false to refuse the call instead.

prompt.description: What to pull from the pages in plain words, such as the version and the release date.

schema.description: The fields to fill, as a JSON Schema object with up to 20 properties. Each is a string, number, integer, boolean, an array, or an object with its own properties, nested up to 4 levels.

scrapeOptions.description: How to read each page, the same options as scrape.

actions.description: Up to 50 steps to run on the page, in order, before reading it: { "type": "wait", "milliseconds": 500 } (up to 30 seconds), { "type": "wait", "selector": ".results" }, { "type": "click", "selector": "button.more" }, { "type": "write", "text": "tides" }, { "type": "press", "key": "Enter" }, { "type": "scroll", "direction": "down" } (also up, left or right; amount is pixels, "viewport" or "max"; maxScrolls 1 to 50; selector scrolls an inner container; "max" keeps scrolling until the page stops growing, for feeds that load as you go), { "type": "screenshot", "fullPage": true } (links come back in actions.screenshots), { "type": "scrape" } (the page at that point, in actions.scrapes), { "type": "executeJavascript", "script": "document.title" } (results in actions.javascriptReturns), { "type": "pdf", "format": "A4" } (links in actions.pdfs) or { "type": "perform", "action": "Click the Load more button" } (a step in plain words, up to 5 browser steps on this page, never leaving the site; at most 5 per call). A read with actions costs 1 credit, the same as any page, and each perform action costs 2 credits more. If an action fails, you still get the page as it stood, with a warning that names the action and says why.

excludeTags.description: Remove the parts of the page that match these CSS selectors, such as .comments.

formats.description: What to return: markdown (clean page text), summary (a short summary of the page), html (the cleaned page), rawHtml (the page as sent), links (every link on the page), images (every image address), screenshot (a link to a JPEG of the visible page, kept for 7 days), changeTracking (what changed in the markdown since your key last read this page with the same options, kept 30 days) network (the JSON the page loaded while it rendered, up to 30 responses) and branding (the page's colors, fonts, typography, spacing, button and input styles, logo and brand images, read from how the page looks, with a field left out when the page does not show it). Send { "type": "screenshot", "fullPage": true } for the whole page. Send { "type": "highlights", "query": "refund policy" } for the passages that best match a query. Send { "type": "json", "schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "price": { "type": "number" } } } } or { "type": "json", "prompt": "the price and the stock" } for fields filled from the page, each checked against it. Send { "type": "json", "parser": "amazon-product" } to get a site's own data as json instead of reading the page; GET /v1/parsers lists the parsers. Send { "type": "json", "rules": { "title": "h1", "links": { "selector": "a", "type": "list", "output": "@href" } } } to read the page with CSS rules and no model, at the page's own price. Send { "type": "attributes", "selectors": [{ "selector": "a", "attribute": "href" }] } for attribute values, returned in attributes. Without a parser or rules, json needs a schema or a prompt and is filled from the page. json with a schema or a prompt, summary and highlights cost 4 credits more each when they return something. json with rules or a parser, and attributes, cost nothing more. A screenshot, network or branding read costs 1 credit, the same as any page. A PDF comes back as markdown only, and costs 1 credit more for each page read.

fullPage.description: Capture the whole page from top to bottom instead of the visible part.

count.description: How many passages to return, best match first.

query.description: What you are looking for on the page, such as refund policy.

options.description: Only with parser: extra inputs for it, such as { "page": 2 } for the next page of results or { "minRating": 4.5 } for a filter. GET /v1/parsers lists what each parser accepts.

parser.description: Read the page with a named parser, which gives the site's own data as json. The url must be the kind of page the parser reads. Parsers are the only way to read some sites. GET /v1/parsers lists them.

prompt.description: What to pull from the page in plain words, such as the version and the release date.

rules.description: Read the page with CSS rules instead of a model, no extra fee. Each field is a selector such as "h1" (the first match's text), "a@href" (an attribute) or { "selector": "li", "type": "list", "output": "text" | "html" | "@attribute" | { nested fields } }. A missing item is null and an unmatched list is []. Relative links become absolute. Up to 100 fields, 5 levels deep. Not with schema, prompt or parser.

schema.description: The fields to fill, as a JSON Schema object with up to 20 properties. Each is a string, number, integer, boolean, an array, or an object with its own properties, nested up to 4 levels.

selectors.description: The elements and attributes to read, such as { selector: 'a.buy', attribute: 'href' }.

includeTags.description: Keep only the parts of the page that match these CSS selectors, such as article or .price. When set, onlyMainContent is not applied.

location.description: Where to read the page from. The default is the United States.

country.description: Two-letter country code to read the page from, such as DE or JP.

maxAge.description: Accept a stored answer up to this many milliseconds old, at most 30 days. Without it, 2 days, or less for a site whose pages change often. 0 always reads the page live. metadata.cacheState says which one you got.

minAge.description: Answer only from a stored copy that is at least this many milliseconds old, and never read the page live. 0 accepts any stored copy. A page with no such copy is notFound.

onlyMainContent.description: Keep only the page's main content, without menus, headers, footers and ads.

parsers.description: Only ["pdf"] is supported: PDFs are read as markdown.

profile.description: Read the page with the cookies and local storage that earlier calls saved under this name, kept for your account for 30 days after the last use. A call with a profile always loads the page in a browser, costs 1 credit, the same as any page, and is never answered from a stored copy. Only one call at a time can save to a profile.

name.description: A name you choose, such as shop-login. Calls with the same name share state.

saveChanges.description: Keep the cookies and local storage this read leaves behind for the next call with this name. Send false to read with the profile without changing it.

storeInCache.description: Send false to neither read nor keep a stored copy of this page.

timeout.description: How long to keep trying, in milliseconds, between 10 seconds and 2 minutes. Pages behind a bot check can need 10 to 30 seconds the first time.

waitFor.description: Extra milliseconds to wait before reading, up to 60000, for pages that load their content late. To wait for an element, add a wait action with a selector. A read that waits costs 1 credit, the same as any page.

zeroDataRetention.description: Send true to keep nothing from this call: no stored copy is read or made, and nothing from it is logged. Costs 1 credit more per page. Not with a screenshot.

urls.description: The pages to read, up to 10, such as ["https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.3"]. With more than one, the fields are filled from all of them together.

zeroDataRetention.description: Send true to keep nothing from this call: pages are read live, the result is held for one hour at most, and nothing is logged. Costs 1 credit more per page.
